about: Layouts of macOS's Preboot list of Recovery administrators, <group>/var/db/AdminUserRecoveryInfo.plist, and what the source-owner proof decides for each. Modes are octal; 'symlink' replaces the item with a symbolic link to a copy; 'missing' removes it. extraLink names the folder that gets a second hard link to the file. content: xml, binary, empty, garbage, array, oversize. Measured layouts name their source, reported layouts come from a person's Installer Log, and the others are synthetic. All values are synthetic test data; no account or volume identifier from any Mac is recorded.

layouts.name: macos-26-measured
layouts.source: Measured read-only on macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), 2026-11-08: group 0777 root, var 0755, var/db 0755, file 0644, 1 link, XML
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: macos-27.2-reported
layouts.source: Reported, not measured: an Installer Log from macOS 27.2 (26B123) after diskutil apfs updatePreboot: group 0755 root, var 0777 root; var/db and the file not shown before the refusal, assumed as on macOS 26
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: second-name-under-shared-var
layouts.source: Synthetic: another hard link to the file in the shared var folder; var/db stays root-only
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: before-macos-26
layouts.source: Synthetic: the protected group folder older macOS versions create
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: sticky-group-folder
layouts.source: Synthetic macOS 27.x candidate: the shared group folder with the sticky bit
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: sticky-db-folder
layouts.source: Synthetic macOS 27.x candidate: var/db shared with the sticky bit
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: second-name-under-protected-folder
layouts.source: Synthetic: another hard link to the file in the shared group folder; var/db stays root-only
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: owner-only-file
layouts.source: Synthetic: the file readable by root alone
layouts.expected: admit

layouts.name: second-name-under-shared-folder
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: a second name in a folder others can write could be a link to another root file
layouts.expected: the file has 2 hard links in a folder others can write

layouts.name: shared-db-folder
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: var/db writable by others without the sticky bit below the shared group folder
layouts.expected: var/db is writable by other users below <group> (mode 0777)

layouts.name: shared-var-and-db-folders
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: var shared as on macOS 27.2 and var/db writable by others too
layouts.expected: var/db is writable by other users below var (mode 0777)

layouts.name: shared-group-and-var-folders
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: only one shared folder per path
layouts.expected: var is writable by other users below <group> (mode 0777)

layouts.name: shared-db-folder-alone
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: the file's own folder is never the shared folder
layouts.expected: var/db is writable by other users (mode 0777)

layouts.name: group-writable-var-under-protected-group
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: only 0777 exactly or the sticky bit is accepted for var

layouts.name: second-name-under-shared-var-db
layouts.source: Synthetic refusal: var shared, var/db sticky, and a second name for the file in var/db
